points.quote: Any usage of GenAI tools in assessments outside what is explicitly permitted will, subject to investigation, be considered a breach of academic integrity, and may lead to disciplinary proceedings in line with RCSI’s Academic Integrity policy.
points.gist: GenAI use in assessments beyond what is explicitly permitted is treated as an academic integrity breach and may lead to disciplinary proceedings.

points.quote: Where GenAI is used, students should include screen captures of both their prompts to and outputs from the GenAI tool as appendices in their submitted work to ensure transparency.
points.gist: Students who use GenAI should include screen captures of prompts and outputs as appendices in their submitted work.

points.quote: Assessments that prohibit or limit the use of GenAI should include a statement for students to declare, e.g. “I have read, understood and abided by the restrictions on the use of Gen AI for this assignment.”
points.gist: Assessments that prohibit or limit GenAI should include a student declaration that they have read and abided by the restrictions.

points.quote: It is the student’s responsibility to confirm that content acquired via GenAI tools is factually correct as these tools are not co-authors and cannot take responsibility for their output.
points.gist: Students are responsible for confirming GenAI content is factually correct, because the tools are not co-authors and cannot take responsibility.

points.quote: the appropriate use of tools that influence only the form of an assessment is generally acceptable (e.g. proof readers, proofreading tools, spelling checkers, thesaurus). However, its use to generate content relating to the substantive aspect of the assessment would generally not be acceptable.
points.gist: Tools affecting only form, such as proofreaders and spelling checkers, are generally acceptable; generating substantive content generally is not.

points.quote: Its use for activities such as brainstorming or outline generation would require consideration on a case-by-case basis.
points.gist: Brainstorming or outline generation with GenAI in assessments is considered case by case.

points.quote: clear written guidance regarding what constitutes acceptable or unacceptable use of GenAI should accompany each assessment.
points.gist: Each assessment should come with clear written guidance on acceptable and unacceptable GenAI use.

points.quote: Personal or proprietary data should only be added to an AI platform, where the privacy of that data is guaranteed, and the explicit permission of the owner has been provided.
points.gist: Personal or proprietary data should only go into an AI platform where its privacy is guaranteed and the owner has explicitly given permission.

points.quote: At present, RCSI’s licence with Microsoft offers commercial data protection to faculty students on the free browser-based Copilot platform.
points.gist: RCSI's Microsoft licence gives commercial data protection on the free browser-based Copilot platform.

points.quote: Uploading personally identifying, institutional, copyrighted or research-related data onto public GenAI platforms may be considered a breach of RCSI’s data privacy protection policy.
points.gist: Uploading personal, institutional, copyrighted or research data to public GenAI platforms may breach RCSI's data privacy policy.

points.quote: It is not advisable to rely on AI detection tools to detect GenAI accurately or reliably.
points.gist: Relying on AI detection tools to detect GenAI accurately or reliably is not advisable.

points.quote: AI detection tools may mis-identify human-written text as AI-generated, leading to unfair accusations of plagiarism. This has been found to be particularly the case for non-native English speakers.
points.gist: Detectors may wrongly flag human-written text as AI-generated, leading to unfair plagiarism accusations, particularly for non-native English speakers.

points.quote: decisions regarding the appropriateness or otherwise of the use of GenAI in education programmes, including assessment processes, are context specific and therefore should not be determined on a whole institution basis.
points.gist: GenAI appropriateness decisions, including for assessment, are context specific and should not be set on a whole-institution basis.

points.quote: Employing follow-up oral examinations where academic integrity breaches are suspected
points.gist: Follow-up oral examinations are suggested where academic integrity breaches are suspected.

points.quote: Where the use of AI is permitted or encouraged, all students should be given access to institutionally approved AI tools.
points.gist: Where AI use is permitted or encouraged, all students should be given access to institutionally approved AI tools.
